question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: The result is the input with each character of ESCAPES replaced by its three-character escape, judged one code unit at a time in a single left-to-right pass. Every other code unit is copied unchanged in its original position; nothing is dropped, added or reordered.

The percent sign is escaped, and it is escaped BEFORE (independently of) the escapes R1 inserts: the "%" that begins an inserted "%0D" or "%0A" is never escaped again. Equivalently each input character maps once, by ESCAPES.

The operation is not idempotent: an input that already contains an escape sequence ("%0A", "%25") has its percent sign escaped again ("%250A", "%2525"). A carriage return and a line feed are escaped separately, so CR LF becomes "%0D%0A".

Only the three characters of ESCAPES are escaped. Colon, comma, equals, "::", tab, the other ASCII controls (NUL, VT, FF), next line (U+0085), line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029), non-ASCII letters, surrogate pairs and unpaired surrogate halves are all copied unchanged. CITED FIDELITY package — colon and comma are escaped by the sibling escape_property (a command PROPERTY value), not here; the toolkit's message escaping is the same three-character set.
